title: Improving the care for people affected by Long/Post-COVID (LCovB) – Survey
summary:
The effects of a Long or Post-COVID illness are enormous for those affected and also for their relatives. It is still not precisely known how many people are affected. Estimates suggest that 5–15% of all SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals are affected. Their care situation is, despite the existence of initial guidelines, partly highly problematic. Outpatient healthcare providers often feel overwhelmed by the treatment. 
By means of comprehensive data collection, the Innovation Fund project "Improving the care for people affected by Long/Post-COVID (LCovB)" aims to determine the prevalence of physician-diagnosed Post-COVID illness and the care situation of people affected by Long/Post-COVID, to identify gaps and barriers in care, and to derive key points for optimizing care – particularly for outpatient care of those severely and persistently ill – supported by an expert panel of professionals and affected persons. 
The overall project is divided into four study modules. 
In study module 2, based on a standardized survey of at least 200 insured persons with Post-COVID illness from three participating company health insurance funds, the following topics will be examined: health status, quality of life, employment situation, everyday activities, Post-COVID symptoms, and care (utilization, barriers, satisfaction). 
The results of the individual study modules will be consolidated. Based on this, recommendations for healthcare practice will be developed jointly with experts.

interventions.name:
This is a non-interventional study. 
A hybrid survey (by post or online, at participants’ choice) will be conducted among individuals with a documented diagnosis of Post-COVID in the reference quarter (expected to be the third quarter of 2024) and in at least one of the three preceding quarters.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Insured persons of 2 participating statutory health insurances: mkk - meine Krankenkasse, Pronova BKK 
Diagnosis U09.9 documented in the reference quarter (expected 3rd quarter 2024) and in at least one of the three previous quarters 
Sufficient German language skills to participate in a structured survey
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals without continuous insurance coverage with a participating statutory health insurance during the observation period, individuals with a protection code (e.g., employees of BKK funds, their family members, or persons under special protection such as those in a police witness protection program), and individuals who have objected to the use of their data for research purposes.
